flowTemplates.name: Welcome sequence
flowTemplates.desc: The first messages a new client receives, on their own clock.

steps.title: Welcome to HAALVING
steps.text:
You are in. HAALVING is not a diet and not a gym — it is **a way of living**, built four pillars at a time: Nutrition, Fitness, Yoga and Mind Wellness.

For the next few days we only watch. No targets, no grading. Log what you already eat and how you already move, and your team reads it before anyone prescribes anything.

steps.title: How we work together
steps.text:
Your circle is one thread. Ask anything in it — a human reads it every day.

We move in **14-day cycles**. Day 12 is your review, day 14 is the meeting where we set what comes next, and days 5 and 10 are rest — they are part of the plan, not a gap in it.

steps.title: Your first week
steps.text:
A week in. The habit that matters most right now is the smallest one you can keep every day.

If something is not working, say so in the thread — a plan you cannot live with is a plan we wrote wrong.

flowTemplates.name: HAALVING healthy-living habits
flowTemplates.desc: One Blue Zones habit a cycle-week, posted on its own.

steps.title: Move naturally
steps.text:
The longest-lived people on earth do not lift weights. They **walk, garden, and climb stairs** all day without calling it exercise.

Today: take the stairs once you would have taken the lift.

steps.title: Eat until you are eighty per cent full
steps.text:
Okinawans say *hara hachi bu* before eating — a reminder to stop at eighty per cent.

Today: put the spoon down when you are no longer hungry, rather than when the plate is empty.

steps.title: Belong to something
steps.text:
Across every Blue Zone, the strongest predictor of a long life was not food or exercise. It was **belonging** — a circle that notices when you are missing.

Today: message one person you have not spoken to in a while. Your Community tab counts too.

gatherings.title: One-day trek to Malayattoor
gatherings.host: Anand walks lead · Sneha packs the plates
gatherings.desc: A gentle 8 km forest trail with the tribe — river crossing, a packed Blue Zones breakfast, and the kind of conversation only a hill can start. All levels welcome; your coach clears your plan for the day.
about: The oldest habit in every Blue Zone is the least glamorous one: people walk, together, on ground that isn’t flat. This is that habit, borrowed for a day. The trail climbs slowly through rubber and forest to the hilltop church — the pace is conversation pace, and the group waits at every fork.

Nobody is graded and nothing syncs to your plan except your steps. Fitness clears the day for you: it counts as your session, and clients with a human Nutrition coach get their plates swapped for the packed breakfast automatically.

agenda.v: Assemble at the pickup point — the bus leaves at 5:45 sharp
Trailhead · briefing, water top-up, phones to silent
River crossing and the packed Blue Zones breakfast
Kurisumudy viewpoint — the long sit, the short photos
Descent · buttermilk stop at the foothill stall
Bus back — home before the evening session

bring: Worn-in walking shoes — not new ones
A hat and a light rain shell
Nothing to eat — the kitchen carries the day

gatherings.title: One-pot Blue Zones cooking session
gatherings.spots: The room is open — enrolling shapes the shopping list
gatherings.desc: Sneha cooks a Sardinian minestrone the HAALVING way — one pot, five vegetables, beans in the lead. Cook along live; the shopping list arrives the evening before.
about: Sardinia’s longest-lived families eat from one pot more days than not. This session is that pot: minestrone the way Seulo cooks it, beans first, vegetables by what the market had, olive oil at the end and never before.

Cook along in your own kitchen with the camera on or off — both are welcome. The recipe scales from one bowl to a family; the swaps for what your plan allows arrive with the shopping list the evening before.

agenda.v: Mise en place together — chop, soak-check, pot on
The cook, live · beans lead, vegetables follow
The swap round — your region’s beans, your plan’s grains
We eat together, cameras optional, seconds encouraged

bring: The shopping list’s vegetables — five is plenty
Beans soaked overnight (the list says which)

about: The easiest session of the month: flat ground, old trees, no pace to keep. We walk in loose clumps that form and reform — the point is as much the talking as the walking. Regulars call it the unofficial progress meeting.
It counts as your steps target for the day, and the buttermilk at the end is on the plan — the filter coffee is between you and your conscience.

challenges.title: 7-day fasting challenge
challenges.host: Set by the dietitian pod · your own coach signs you in
challenges.stake: A fasting ring on your Journey — and lighter mornings
challenges.desc: A gentle overnight fast: dinner done by 8, breakfast at 10 — a 14-hour pause your body spends housekeeping. No skipped meals, no heroics; your coach adjusts if your plan needs it.
about: Every Blue Zone eats across a short day without calling it fasting — supper early, breakfast late, and the night left to the body’s housekeeping. This challenge borrows exactly that and nothing more: fourteen quiet hours, seven nights.

Nothing about your plates changes — the same food, moved closer together. Clients on medication or with flagged markers get a coach call before day one; the panel adjusts the window rather than dropping you out.
how: Dinner finished by 8 PM — finished, not started
Breakfast from 10 AM, as your plan already writes it
Water, plain herbal tea and black coffee stay open all night
Miss a night? Log it and carry on — streaks bend, they don’t break
On medication: your coach confirms your window before day one

arc.v: The fidgety window — the 9 PM habit argues back. Warm water wins.
The quiet stretch — hunger arrives on schedule and leaves politely.
The settled mornings — most people report the first one here.

challenges.title: 10k steps · 11 days
challenges.host: The fitness pod referees · the tribe board keeps score
challenges.stake: The walker’s crown on the tribe board, held till someone takes it
challenges.desc: Ten thousand steps a day for one full cycle. The tribe board keeps everyone’s week side by side — walk together, even apart.
about: Ten thousand is not a magic number — it is simply far enough that it cannot happen by accident. Hitting it daily for a whole cycle means the walking found places to live in your day: the call you take on your feet, the stop before your stop, the after-dinner loop.

Your tracker syncs the board each night, and the board shows the tribe side by side — not to shame the short days, but because a row of other people’s green squares is the best walking shoe ever made.
how: Your own watch or phone counts — the board syncs at midnight
Active-rest days keep an 8k floor, the plan says which days those are
Rain, travel, deadlines — log the honest number; the board carries context chips
Three short days in a row and your fitness coach checks in — help, not homework

arc.v: Find your slots — where the steps actually fit your day.
Protect the evening walk — the slot every miss has in common.
Hold it without thinking. That is the whole point.

challenges.title: Table before eight
challenges.host: The whole tribe, honour system · confessions welcome in the feed
challenges.stake: A Table ring — and your sleep tracker’s quiet gratitude
challenges.desc: Dinner on the table and done by 8 PM for one cycle. Late plates make honest confessions in the feed.
about: The earliest habit HAALVING borrows from the Blue Zones is the early table: supper done while the sky is still lighter than the room. Digestion gets its evening, sleep gets its full night, and tomorrow’s breakfast gets an appetite.
This one runs on the honour system. No tracker watches your table — the feed does. Late plates make the best posts, and the tribe has never once been unkind to a confession.
how: Dinner served AND finished by 8 PM
A photo to the meal queue if you like — the dietitian reads it either way
Miss a night, post the story — a samosa at 9:40 has friends here
Eleven nights, one cycle — the review meeting sees the pattern, not the slips

arc.v: The scramble — dinner argues with traffic and the fridge.
The 8 PM reflex forms — the kitchen starts earlier on its own.
The sleep dividend lands — mornings vote to keep the habit.

qs.q: How do the longest-lived communities move?
opts: Natural movement woven through the day
qs.why: Gardens, walking, kneading, climbing — movement lives inside the day, not beside it.

qs.q: Hara hachi bu, the Okinawan table rule, means…
qs.why: Stopping at 80% gives the stomach its twenty-minute head start on the brain.

qs.q: The strongest dinner habit for deeper sleep?
qs.why: Digesting and deep sleep compete — an early plate hands the night to sleep.

qs.q: What do nearly all documented centenarians share?
qs.why: Ikigai, plan de vida — a reason to wake up adds years, and years add reasons.

qs.q: Your circle of friends most strongly shapes…
qs.why: Habits are contagious — the tribe you keep is the diet you keep.

qs.q: A ten-minute walk after meals mainly helps…
qs.why: Working muscles drink up glucose, so the after-meal rise stays gentle.

qs.q: Which fats anchor Blue Zones plates?
qs.why: Sardinia and Ikaria run on olive oil and nuts — fats that carry the vegetables.

qs.q: Beans in the Blue Zones are eaten…
qs.why: The world’s longevity all-star food is the humble, daily bowl of beans.

qs.q: Screens late at night mostly disturb…
qs.why: Bright light tells the brain it is still daytime, so the sleep signal comes late.

qs.q: Water before a meal supports…
qs.why: A glass before the plate takes the edge off hunger and slows the fork.

qs.q: A downshift practice is…
opts: A short daily pause that lowers stress
qs.why: Every Blue Zone has one — prayer, naps, tea, remembering ancestors. Stress needs a valve.

qs.q: Whole grains beat refined ones mainly because…
qs.why: Intact fibre slows the sugar and feeds the gut — milling it away leaves just the spike.

qs.q: Okinawan elders keep gardens because they give…
opts: Purpose, movement and greens in one
qs.why: One plot delivers a reason to rise, a daily bend-and-carry, and dinner.

qs.q: The Sardinian shepherds’ movement secret was…
qs.why: Five gentle uphill miles a day, most days, for a lifetime — no gym required.

qs.q: Eating with company tends to make meals…
qs.why: Conversation is a natural pause button — the table fills before the plate refills.

qs.q: Caffeine after mid-afternoon mainly costs you…
qs.why: Half of a 3 PM coffee is still circulating at 9 PM, quietly shaving the deep stages.

qs.q: Morning sunlight helps because it…
opts: Sets the body clock for the day
qs.why: Ten bright minutes anchor the rhythm that decides tonight’s sleepiness.

qs.q: Protein works best for muscle when…
qs.why: Muscle listens at every meal — even portions beat one flood.

qs.q: A slow exhale calms you because it…
opts: Speaks to the calming half of the nervous system
qs.why: A longer out-breath is the body’s own brake pedal — free and always installed.

qs.q: The healthiest snack habit in the Zones is…
qs.why: Nut eaters live measurably longer — a small handful, most days.

qs.q: NEAT — the movement that adds up most — is…
qs.why: The day’s ordinary motion burns more than the gym hour for most people.

qs.q: Added sugar is best kept…
qs.why: Roughly six teaspoons — beyond that the liver starts bottling the excess.

qs.q: Fermented foods like curd and kanji mainly feed…
qs.why: Live cultures keep the gut’s garden diverse — and the gut talks to everything.

qs.q: A simple gratitude habit measurably improves…
qs.why: Three written lines a night lower rumination — the mind unclenches before bed.

qs.q: The best hydration signal to trust is…
qs.why: The body posts its own gauge twice — listen rather than count.

fitness.name: Brisk walk intervals
fitness.instructions:
Walk two minutes briskly — the pace where talking takes effort but is still possible.
Drop to an easy stroll for one minute. Let the breath come back on its own.
Repeat that pair for the whole session. The pace changes train the heart, not the distance.
Finish on an easy minute rather than a hard one.

fitness.name: Chair squats
fitness.instructions:
Stand in front of a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width apart, arms loose at your sides.
Push your hips back as though you were about to sit, and lower until you lightly touch the seat.
Press through your heels to stand tall again, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up. Ten of those, then rest.
fitness.caution: Skip if knee pain — reduce depth and hold the chair.

fitness.name: Wall push-ups
fitness.instructions: Place your palms on a wall at shoulder height, step back until your body is at a slight angle, then bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall and press back out.

fitness.name: Glute bridge
fitness.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, then squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders.

fitness.name: Step-ups
fitness.instructions: Step fully onto a sturdy step or low bench with one foot, drive through the heel to stand tall, then step back down with control.

fitness.name: Goblet squats
fitness.instructions: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell close to your chest with both hands, then squat down between your knees and drive back up through your heels.
fitness.caution: Keep a neutral spine throughout — don’t round or arch the lower back under load.

fitness.name: Resistance-band rows
fitness.instructions: Anchor the band at chest height, step back to create tension, and pull the handles toward your ribs while squeezing your shoulder blades together.

fitness.name: Plank hold
fitness.instructions: Rest on your forearms and toes with your body in one straight line from head to heels, and hold while breathing steadily.

fitness.name: Farmer carry
fitness.instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand and walk tall for the stated distance, keeping your shoulders back and core braced.

fitness.name: Kettlebell swings
fitness.instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hinge at the hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs, then drive your hips forward to swing it to chest height.
fitness.caution: This is a hip hinge, not a squat — drive through the hips and keep the knees soft.

fitness.name: Tempo run
fitness.instructions: Run at a pace that’s comfortably hard — one where a full sentence is difficult but a few words are still possible — for the stated duration.

fitness.name: Push-up ladder
fitness.instructions: Do one push-up, rest a few seconds, then two, then three, climbing the ladder as high as clean form allows before starting back down.

yoga.name: Cat–Cow
yoga.instructions: On hands and knees, inhale as you drop your belly and lift your chest and tailbone (Cow), then exhale as you round your spine toward the ceiling (Cat).

yoga.name: Uttanasana forward fold
yoga.instructions: From standing, hinge at the hips and fold forward, letting your head and arms hang heavy toward the floor.
yoga.caution: Keep a soft bend in the knees, and rise slowly if you have low blood pressure.

yoga.name: Baddha Konasana
yoga.instructions: Sit tall, bring the soles of your feet together, and let your knees drop toward the floor while you hold your ankles.

yoga.name: Surya Namaskar A
yoga.instructions:
Stand at the front of your mat, palms together at the heart, and take one steady breath.
Inhale the arms overhead; exhale and fold forward from the hips.
Inhale to a halfway lift, exhale and step or jump back to plank.
Lower through chaturanga, inhale to upward dog, exhale to downward dog. Hold five breaths.
Walk or jump the feet back in, rise to standing, and begin the next round.

yoga.name: Trikonasana
yoga.instructions: Step your feet wide, turn one foot out, and reach that hand down toward your shin or the floor while the other arm reaches up.

yoga.name: Warrior II
yoga.instructions: Step your feet wide, bend the front knee to a right angle, and stretch your arms out parallel to the floor while gazing over your front hand.

yoga.name: Bridge pose
yoga.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent, press through your feet to lift your hips, and clasp your hands beneath you if that’s comfortable.

yoga.name: Crow prep
yoga.instructions: Squat low, place your hands shoulder-width apart on the floor, and lean your weight forward onto your hands, lifting one foot and then the other to tap your knees onto your upper arms.
yoga.caution: Warm up the wrists first, and come out immediately if you feel any wrist pain.

yoga.name: Headstand prep
yoga.instructions: Interlace your fingers on the floor, place the crown of your head between your hands, and walk your feet in to lift your hips overhead against a wall.
yoga.caution: Never attempt your first headstand unsupervised — practice against a wall with a coach or experienced partner nearby.

yoga.name: Yoga-nidra wind-down
yoga.instructions: Lie down in Savasana and follow a guided body scan from toes to head, staying awake but completely still and relaxed.

culture.name: Idli
culture.instructions:
Steam the idlis until a knife comes out clean — about ten minutes on a rolling boil.
Serve them hot. An idli left to cool goes dense, and half the point is the lightness.
Pair with sambar and a spoon of chutney; skip the extra oil.

culture.name: Coconut chutney
culture.instructions: Serve fresh alongside idli or dosa as a small side — a couple of tablespoons is plenty.

culture.name: Plain dosa
culture.instructions: Cook the fermented batter thin and crisp on a hot griddle, and serve plain or with a light vegetable filling.

culture.name: Sambar
culture.instructions: Simmer toor dal with tamarind, sambar powder and mixed vegetables until the lentils soften into a thick, tangy stew.

culture.name: Oats bowl
culture.instructions: Cook rolled oats in water or low-fat milk and top with fruit or a spoon of nuts for a fibre-rich start to the day.

culture.name: Moong-dal cheela
culture.instructions: Blend soaked moong dal into a thick batter, season with ginger and green chilli, and cook thin on a hot griddle like a savoury pancake.

culture.name: Grilled paneer salad
culture.instructions:
Grill the paneer cubes on a hot dry pan until lightly charred on two sides.
Build the bed first — mixed greens, cucumber, tomato — then lay the paneer over it warm.
Dress with lemon and a pinch of salt. No creamy dressing; it undoes the point of the dish.

culture.name: Curd rice
culture.instructions: Mash cooked rice with fresh curd, temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves, and serve cool as a gut-settling finish to the meal.

culture.name: Ragi porridge
culture.instructions: Whisk ragi flour into water or low-fat milk and simmer until thick, sweetening lightly with jaggery if needed.

culture.name: Sprouts chaat
culture.instructions: Toss steamed moong and matki sprouts with chopped onion, tomato, lemon juice and chaat masala for a crunchy, protein-rich snack.

culture.name: Vegetable upma
culture.instructions: Roast semolina until fragrant, then simmer with sautéed vegetables and water until it comes together soft and fluffy.

culture.name: Buttermilk
culture.instructions: Whisk chilled curd with water, a pinch of roasted cumin and salt, and serve cold as a light, cooling drink with meals.

wellness.name: Box breathing 5 min
wellness.instructions: Inhale for a count of four, hold for four, exhale for four, and hold empty for four — repeat the square for five minutes.

wellness.name: Yoga nidra 20 min
wellness.instructions:
Lie on your back somewhere warm, legs a little apart, palms turned up.
Let the breath settle on its own. Nothing to lengthen, nothing to count.
Follow the guided scan from the feet upward, resting attention on each part as it is named.
If you drift off, that is not a failure — the practice has done its work.

wellness.name: Digital downshift hour
wellness.instructions: Switch off screens for the hour before bed and swap them for reading, stretching or quiet conversation to let your mind settle.

wellness.name: Gratitude journal
wellness.instructions: Write down three specific things that went well today, however small, before you put the day to rest.

wellness.name: Body scan 10 min
wellness.instructions: Lie down and bring your attention slowly through each part of your body in turn, noticing tension and consciously releasing it.

wellness.name: 4-7-8 breath
wellness.instructions: Inhale quietly through your nose for four counts, hold for seven, and exhale slowly through your mouth for eight — repeat four rounds.

wellness.name: Walk without phone
wellness.instructions: Take a walk of at least fifteen minutes leaving your phone behind, and let your attention rest on your surroundings instead of a screen.

wellness.name: Wind-down routine
wellness.instructions: Follow the same simple sequence every night — dim the lights, stretch gently, and note tomorrow’s one priority — so your body learns bedtime is near.

motivation.name: The village that eats together
motivation.instructions: The people who live longest almost never eat alone. Ninety seconds on the table as the oldest health technology we have.

motivation.name: What a hundred-year-old plate looks like
motivation.instructions: Not a diet — a shape. Beans, greens, grains and whatever grew nearby, on repeat for eighty years.

motivation.name: Movement you never scheduled
motivation.instructions: Nobody in a Blue Zone goes to the gym. They garden, they walk to the shop, they sit on the floor. Why that beats an hour of effort.

motivation.name: The eighty per cent rule
motivation.instructions: Hara hachi bu — the Okinawan habit of stopping when you are eighty per cent full, and the twenty minutes your stomach needs to tell your brain.

motivation.name: The first breath of the day
motivation.instructions: Four counts in, four held, four out. What a single square of breathing does to a nervous system that woke up already behind.

motivation.name: The hour before you sleep
motivation.instructions: Sleep is not what happens after the day ends — it is built in the sixty minutes before it does.

motivation.name: Ikigai — a reason to get up
motivation.instructions: The Okinawan word for the thing that gets you out of bed. Seven years of life expectancy sit in the answer.

motivation.name: Why muscle is a savings account
motivation.instructions: What you build in your forties is what you spend in your seventies. The most honest argument for lifting anything at all.

motivation.name: The sweetness you did not choose
motivation.instructions: Blue Zone diets are not sugar-free — they are sugar-honest. On the difference between a festival sweet and a daily one.

motivation.name: Downshift
motivation.instructions: Every long-lived culture has a ritual for shedding the day — a nap, a prayer, a walk, a glass on the porch. Stress is the same everywhere; the routine is what differs.

motivation.name: The five people around you
motivation.instructions: Moai — the lifelong circle of friends an Okinawan is placed in at birth. Your habits are, statistically, an average of theirs.

motivation.name: The first glass
motivation.instructions: Nobody in a Blue Zone counts litres. They keep water within arm’s reach and the counting takes care of itself.

motivation.name: The errand that became exercise
motivation.instructions: The longest-lived people on earth do not go to a gym. Their villages are built so that the shortest route to anything is on foot.

motivation.name: Doing nothing, properly
motivation.instructions: Rest is not the absence of the programme — it is a part of it that happens to feel like a reward.
